minor.issue: Auth is cookie-only (`retailer_session` via fastapi Cookie(...)); Authorization: Bearer <token> returns 401 even though /api/retailer-auth/login hands back a `token` in the JSON body. Since the cookie is issued with secure=True samesite=none, any non-HTTPS client (curl/requests/pytest against http://localhost:8001) silently loses the session. Consider also accepting `Authorization: Bearer` on the retailer dashboard dependency so the JSON `token` is actually usable, or gate `secure` on an env flag for non-prod.

KEY GOTCHA for any retailer-authenticated test: /api/retailer-auth/login sets `retailer_session` with secure=True, so requests.Session() stores but never replays it over http://localhost:8001 -> every subsequent /api/retailer-dashboard/* call 401s. rca_of_the_issue: After the main agent's seed fix, TestB2BCatalog no longer skipped but FAILED with 401 'Not authenticated' on GET /api/retailer-dashboard/b2b/catalog. Root cause was NOT the fix: routers/retailer_auth.py sets the `retailer_session` cookie with secure=True, and routers/retailer_dashboard.py reads auth exclusively from that cookie. Python `requests` honours the Secure attribute and refuses to send the cookie over plain http://localhost:8001, so the session was anonymous. Proof: `curl -H 'Cookie: retailer_session=<token from login body>' .../b2b/catalog` returns HTTP 200 with the full catalog, while `-H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>'` returns 401. Mitigation applied (in test scope only): the test now reads `token` from the login JSON and passes it as an explicit Cookie header, and uses pytest.fail instead of pytest.skip so a real auth break can never be silently masked again. No application code was changed.
